plain.li: Smooth on one side and rough on the other, that's a keeper.
I'll know the right one when I see it.
[winter] Cold as ice, but look at the colour in it.
[old] I've a box of these at home older than some of you.

warm.li: This one's for the windowsill, so somebody gets the morning on it.

blunt.li: Not that one, not that one, that one.

cheerful.li: Treasure, everywhere you look, if you look.

gloomy.li: Every stone here has been here longer than any of us will be.

cold.li: Mostly the same grey stone, and one that isn't.

plain.li: Follow the grain and it does half the work for you.
Nearly lost a thumb on that knot, there.
[evening] A bit of wood and a quiet hour, that's my evening.
[old] My hands shake for everything except this.

warm.li: I'll give this one to whoever smiles at it first.

cheerful.li: It was going to be a fox, it's turning out a dog, and that's fine.

gloomy.li: It never comes out like the one in my head.

cold.li: A useful way to keep the hands busy.

plain.li: Crumbs here, and seed for the shy ones over there.
Don't fight over it, there's plenty.
[summer] Thirsty, are you, in this heat?
[rain] Wet feathers, all of you, poor things.

cheerful.li: Here they come, the whole noisy lot of them!

cold.li: Same birds, same time, every day, very orderly of them.

plain.li: The work can spare me for the length of a cloud.
Face up, eyes shut, and nobody ask me anything.
[spring] First real warmth in the sun this year.
[old] Old bones like the sun best.

warm.li: There's warmth enough out here for everybody, come on.

cold.li: Ten minutes of this and I'll work better all afternoon.

plain.li: Everything goes quiet when it snows, have you noticed?
Flakes on my sleeve, look, every one a little star.
[old] I've seen a lot of snow and I'm still not tired of it.

warm.li: Come and stand in it a minute, it does you good.

gloomy.li: Snow on my face, and for a minute nothing's wrong.

plain.li: A place for everything, if people would only use it.
Somebody left their cup here, and I know it isn't mine.
Straighten this, sweep that, and it's a room again.

cheerful.li: Look at that, you could eat off it now.

cold.li: Clutter slows everyone down, so it goes.

plain.li: Quiet now, and the whole day still to come.
[fall] Mist in the low ground and the light coming through it.
[spring] Lighter every morning now, you can feel the year turning.

warm.li: Good morning to you, sun, and to everyone still asleep.

plain.li: Steady strokes, and listen for the change in the sound.
Who's been chopping roots with this, honestly?
[afterraid] After a fight every blade wants seeing to.

warm.li: I'll do yours next, if you leave it on the bench.

cheerful.li: Sharp enough to split a hair, nearly.

plain.li: The wind's from the west, so that's where I'll look.
Our own boot prints, mostly, going out and coming back.
[snow] Fresh snow tells you everything that walked past.

cheerful.li: Every path out here has a story, if you read it.

cold.li: No new tracks since yesterday, as expected.

plain.li: A light in the dark is a kindness that costs almost nothing.
A light by the door, so nobody walks past us in the dark.
[rain] Rain or not, the light stays where it can be seen.

warm.li: Whoever's out there, there's a light here for you.

gloomy.li: Maybe nobody will see it tonight, but it'll be lit.

plain.li: A quick look along every row, then breakfast.
[spring] The new shoots look strong this morning.
[fall] Nearly ready, and nothing's getting it before we do.

cheerful.li: Every leaf accounted for, good morning, plants.

gloomy.li: I lost a crop once, and I'm not losing another.

plain.li: Breathe through the nose, slow, and let the cold go past.
Mittens on, hood up, and no standing about.
[snow] Snow's soft today, so I'll keep to the packed path.

blunt.li: Cold, fine, I'm ready for it.

cold.li: Do it the way you were taught and the cold is only weather.
